objectives: Identify passive voice verb phrases in a short text [fk.g.passive]
Form simple passive sentences using be + past participle [fk.g.passive]
Understand a short spoken and written text containing passive structures [fk.k.hoer.1, fk.k.lesen.1]
Open, continue, and close a short conversation using at least 3 target phrases [fk.w.open_continue_close_conversations, fk.k.sprechen.1]

stages.name: Opening: Retrieval + Bridge + I can
stages.purpose: Activate pupils' knowledge of normal English word order and past participle forms, then bridge to today's passive-voice target.

procedure.text: Quick fire: 4 oral recognition items — a subject-verb-object sentence, past participle forms (cleaned/explained/given), a greeting phrase, a farewell phrase.
Think-write: students write 2 active sentences about school.
Check: partner swap.
Bridge: teacher connects normal word order to passive — 'Today we flip it: the thing that receives the action comes first.'
I can on board: I can identify passive sentences. I can change an active sentence to a passive one. I can open and close a conversation with 3 phrases.

stages.name: Input: Back at School text
stages.purpose: Give pupils a passive-heavy listening and reading model before they have to produce it themselves.

procedure.text: Pre-teach 3 new words from the glossary: caretaker, form teacher, timetable.
Teacher reads 'Back at School' text aloud while students listen with books closed [fk.k.hoer.1].
Students then read the text independently and underline the passive verb phrases (is cleaned, are given, are explained) [fk.k.lesen.1].
Together: check the underlined phrases.
Show the passive-voice explanation and compare it against the underlined phrases.
Brief Q&A: what action happens? who does it?

stages.name: Guided practice: passive forms
stages.purpose: Move from recognition to guided production of passive forms in three escalating steps.

procedure.text: Explain the three tasks and the formula card (is/are + past participle).
(1) Mark the passive verb: click every passive verb phrase in the sentences — recognition only.
(2) Gap-fill: complete 6 passive sentences using the hint word — near-transfer.
(3) Reorder: unscramble 4 passive sentences from shuffled fragments — guided production. Weaker pupils keep the formula card; stronger pupils must add a by-phrase. [fk.g.passive]
Check answers together.

stages.name: Conversation phrases + speaking
stages.purpose: Pre-teach and then practice functional phrases for opening, continuing, and closing a conversation.

procedure.text: Pre-teach 8 phrases in 3 groups using the glossary (3 open, 3 continue, 2 close).
Students copy the phrases into their notebook.
Pairs match each phrase to its function (open/continue/close) using the matching exercise.
Pairs practice a scripted 6-line dialogue using one phrase from each group. Rotate partners once. [fk.w.open_continue_close_conversations, fk.k.sprechen.1]
Two pairs perform their dialogue for the class.

stages.name: Wrap-up
stages.purpose: Quick formative check against today's I-can statements before dismissing.

procedure.text: Return to the I-can statements — thumbs up/sideways/down per statement.
Teacher notes any thumbs-down on passive production. Preview: exercises and flashcards posted as homework practice.

differentiationNotes: Weaker: formula card (is/are + past participle), word bank visible throughout practice, scripted dialogue card for speaking phase. Stronger: no word bank for transformation task, must include by + agent phrase, can improvise dialogue beyond script.
exercisePlan: mark_the_words — click every passive verb phrase in 6 sentences [fk.g.passive]
gap_fill — complete 6 passive sentences with correct be + past participle form, hint word provided [fk.g.passive]
reorder — unscramble 4 passive sentences from shuffled fragments [fk.g.passive]
matching — match 8 conversation phrases to their function (open/continue/close) [fk.w.open_continue_close_conversations]
flashcards — 8 conversation phrase flashcards for self-study [fk.w.open_continue_close_conversations]
